verdictBasis: The repair selects the important TypeScript topology, package closure, host authority split, broad process fate, and the external-scanner D9 rejection, and the implementer blueprint now reflects that process choice. It is not seal-ready on the reviewed snapshot. Protocol-major 1 has no closed payload schema for any named TypeScript frame, so the Rust host and JavaScript worker still have to invent their cross-process API and the semantics of one Analyze shared by several logical stages. The retained DELIVERY checker also accepts removal or contradiction of several load-bearing TypeScript rules. For the scanner overlay, the rejection reason and D9 mapping are exact, but its RequestId-may-exist outcome conflicts with live REQUEST-ID-V1, which requires RequestId before every request-validation rejection. Both IP-R4-03 and IP-R4-05 therefore remain OPEN on this snapshot. These are architecture/design-integrity findings; no product implementation or release behavior was evaluated or demonstrated.

findingDispositions.progress: The binding DELIVERY artifact now selects a bundled release-pinned Node worker, signed runtime/provider packages, absolute launch, a one-shot per-universe lifetime, sealed-VFS inherited-pipe transport, host-only durability/policy authority, TCB-not-sandbox posture, identity closure, and broad D9 failure fates. Those choices remove the embedded-versus-worker and ambient-runtime architecture forks.
whyStillOpen: Protocol-major 1 enumerates frame names and prose ordering but has no closed payload schema for Hello, OpenUniverse, Snapshot*, Analyze, FactBatch, Coverage or terminal frames. The Rust and JavaScript implementations must invent field names/types, unknown-field handling, request/stage correlation and exact cross-contract payload joins.

The process model says all TypeScript stages for a universe share one child while the protocol permits one Analyze, but it does not bind whether Analyze carries one union request, an ordered stage list, per-stage budgets, or how FactBatch/Coverage attribution closes. That is cross-process behavior, not a local serializer choice.
The retained checker accepts deletion or contradiction of protocol ordering, unavailable/budget fates, process ownership, network posture and offline assets.

findings.title: Protocol-major 1 names frames but does not bind their payload schemas or multi-stage semantics
findings.statement: typescriptSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol has transport, major, two frame-name arrays, prose ordering and prose Snapshot transport, but no frameSchemas or equivalent closed wire objects. In particular OpenUniverse, Analyze, FactBatch, Coverage and terminal frames have no required/optional fields or exact references to the live semantic-universe, fact and Coverage contracts. One Analyze is required even though all stages for a universe share the child, without a binding aggregation/attribution rule.
findings.impact: The Rust host and JavaScript worker must jointly invent a versioned cross-language API during implementation. Independent implementations can disagree while both appear to follow the architecture; stage budgets, result attribution, completeness and protocol-fault classification can diverge.

findings.title: DL-TS checker coverage is narrower than its load-bearing claim
findings.statement: R5-PROBE-01 through R5-PROBE-08 all escaped. The checker validates selected substrings and descriptor sets but not the complete TypeScript object, protocol state machine, clean unavailable/budget fates, ownership, network rule or offline asset closure.
findings.impact: A later contract edit can silently reopen the topology and fate choices while normal and retained selftests stay green. Green status cannot protect the adjudication as claimed.

findings.title: Scanner RequestId fate conflicts with live REQUEST-ID-V1
findings.statement: DELIVERY says RequestId may exist for an external-scanner rejection. OPERABILITY requires a host-minted, reserved RequestId immediately at first trusted ingress for every request, including requests later rejected during parsing or request validation. The scanner check occurs after request validation inputs have been resolved, so optional RequestId is impossible under the live identity contract.
findings.impact: The exact pre-attempt outcome is cross-contract inconsistent. An implementation following DELIVERY may omit RequestId and violate event/audit/budget identity; one following OPERABILITY will contradict the provider adjudication.

findings.title: DL-SCOPE does not guard the live RequestId join or contradictory admission prose
findings.statement: R5-PROBE-09 and R5-PROBE-10 escaped. The checker verifies post-admission identity absence and the isolated overlay decision but does not cross-check RequestId with OPERABILITY or require the aggregate admission rule to agree with the overlay.
findings.impact: The machine check can report the scanner outcome clean while the public architecture contains incompatible admission behavior.
